chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Ali ibn Ibrahim from his father from Ibn Abi Abi Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabi from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
Indeed, the Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'Every beast with fangs and every bird with talons is forbidden.' And he said: 'Do not eat anything from the beasts of prey.'
ai.seo_question: What are the physical characteristics that make an animal forbidden to eat according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) codifies the prohibition of *al-siba'* (beasts of prey) and *al-tair* (birds of prey) by linking their physical traits—fangs and talons—to ritual impurity. This ruling forms a cornerstone of Shia dietary law, distinguishing between clean and unclean animals based on prophetic tradition and juristic deduction.
